src/application/create-user-use-case.ts: `if (typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === "") { throw new ValidationError("name is required"); }`. This repeats the same name rule inline instead of keeping it in one place.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module is cohesive: one use-case class per file, each taking DTOs from dtos.ts and domain repositories. But there are two problems. (1) ListTasksUseCase has a validateExecute(dto: CreateProjectDto) method that calls assertExecuteRule, which create-project-use-case.ts exports. Project-creation validation has nothing to do with listing tasks. This also turns a private rule of one use case into an exported helper that another use case depends on. (2) The rule that a name is a non-empty, trimmed string appears twice. It is in assertExecuteRule in create-project-use-case.ts and again inline in CreateUserUseCase.execute in create-user-use-case.ts. Even though assertExecuteRule is now a shared export, CreateUserUseCase does not use it.

violations.message: ListTasksUseCase.validateExecute(dto: CreateProjectDto) calls assertExecuteRule from create-project-use-case.ts. This mixes project-creation validation into a task-listing use case and couples two unrelated use cases.
assertExecuteRule, a validation rule private to CreateProjectUseCase, is exported and used by ListTasksUseCase. The use-case boundary leaks.

CreateUserUseCase.execute repeats the name rule (`typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === ""` → ValidationError("name is required")) that assertExecuteRule in create-project-use-case.ts already defines, so the rule lives in two places.
